payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_probe_check.py::test_the_inert_patterns_note_obeys_claude_mds_sentence_limit_by_hand stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to .saffron/gates/prose.py. The claim was "`tests/test_probe_check.py:725` holds a bare string statement, directly below `INERT_PATTERNS`'s closing paren at `tests/test_probe_check.py:724`. `.saffron/gates/prose.py:275`'s `_documented` walks a parsed module for `ast.Module`, `ast.FunctionDef`, `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` and `ast.ClassDef` nodes only (`.saffron/gates/prose.py:272`), and keeps a node only where `ast.get_docstring` finds one (`.saffron/gates/prose.py:282-286`). A bare statement following an assignment is none of those, so `_python_prose` never reads its text and the `prose` gate never sees it. Its second sentence, at `tests/test_probe_check.py:726`, runs twenty-six words long, and `CLAUDE.md:238` states the limit for new comments as twenty-five. The note's sentences are reworded so each stays within that limit, with its meaning unchanged. A new test reads the note from this file's own source with `ast.parse` and asserts every one of its sentences stays within the limit by hand, so a later rewrite that grows one past it fails here instead of passing unseen.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
